app.name: Alpine OTA Updater
intro.title: Update your MeshCore node over the air
intro.lead: Pick the device and firmware, download it once, then send it to the node over Bluetooth or WiFi. Downloaded files stay on this device for later.
step.label: Step {n}:
board.hint: Choose the hardware of the node you want to update.
board.search: Search devices, e.g. RAK, T114, Heltec V3

source.extend: More firmware sources can be added in catalog/sources.json.
sourceDesc.powersaving: MeshCore with power-saving and experimental features, by IoTThinks.
sourceDesc.zephcore: MeshCore-compatible firmware built on Zephyr RTOS, by liquidraver.

connect.ble.title: Put the node into update mode
connect.ble.step.1: In your companion app, log in to the node as admin.
connect.ble.step.2: Send the command start ota. The node appears as {name}. A node already in bootloader (DFU) mode also works.
connect.ble.step.3: Keep this device within a few metres of the node, press Scan and select the node.
connect.wifi.title: Connect to the node's WiFi
connect.wifi.step.1: In your companion app, log in to the node as admin and send start ota. It replies with “Started: {url}”.
connect.wifi.step.2: Open the WiFi settings of this device and join the open network {ssid}.
connect.wifi.step.3: If the device warns that the network has no internet, choose to stay connected.
connect.wifi.step.4: Come back to this app and press Scan.
connect.wifi.offlineNote: The node's WiFi has no internet. Download the firmware before you switch networks; this app works offline. On a phone, turn off mobile data during the update so the app talks to the node's WiFi.

flash.notReady: Select a firmware and a node first.
flash.before: The update takes a few minutes. Keep this device close to the node and this page open until it finishes.
flash.cancelled: Update cancelled. The node may stay in update mode; start the update again or restart the node.
flash.error: The update failed. The node stays in update mode, so you can try again.
flash.keepOpen: Do not close this page or let the device sleep until the update finishes.
flash.mismatch: The node calls itself {name}, which belongs to: {boards}. You selected {board}. Flashing the wrong firmware can make the node unusable until it is reflashed over USB.
flash.unknown: The node calls itself {name}, so it cannot be checked whether it is a {board}. Make sure the firmware matches the hardware.
flash.stage.entering-bootloader: Restarting the node into update mode
flash.doneText: The node is restarting with firmware {version}. Check it with the ver command in your companion app.
flash.prnHint: Lower values are slower but more reliable. Default: 32. 0 turns confirmations off.
firmware.appOnly: Downloading needs the installed app. In a browser, only the release list is shown.
connect.noneInUpdateMode: No node in update mode found. Check step 2 above, then scan again.
connect.pressScan: Press Scan to look for nodes in update mode.
connect.appOnly: Bluetooth updates need the installed app.
connect.error.permission: Bluetooth permission was denied. Allow it in the system settings and try again.
connect.error.adapter-off: Bluetooth is turned off. Turn it on and try again.
flash.compatHint: Use if the update fails right after it starts. Much slower.
connect.appOnlyWifi: WiFi updates need the installed app.
connect.error.unreachable: No node answers. Check that this device is connected to the {ssid} WiFi and that the node is still in update mode.
flash.unknownWifi: The node reports its board as “{reported}”, which could not be matched to {board}. Make sure the firmware matches the hardware.
flash.doneTextWifi: The node accepted firmware {version} and is restarting. Reconnect this device to your normal WiFi, then check the version with the ver command in your companion app.
flash.zephcoreFirstBoot: If this node currently runs Arduino MeshCore (official or PowerSaving), ZephCore may reformat its storage on the first start: node name, admin password, radio settings and possibly the node identity can be reset. Do this switch only on a node you can reach and reconfigure. Updating ZephCore to a newer ZephCore keeps the settings.
err.timeout: The device did not answer in time.
err.network: Network error. Check the connection and try again.
err.http: The server answered with an error (HTTP {status}).
err.storage: Not enough storage, or the file cannot be saved.
err.fwMissing: The firmware file is no longer in the library. Download it again.
err.github.rateLimit: GitHub is temporarily limiting requests. Wait a few minutes and try again.
err.ble.noAdapter: No Bluetooth adapter found. Check that this device has Bluetooth and that it is turned on.
err.ble.off: Bluetooth is turned off. Turn it on and try again.
err.ble.permission: The app has no Bluetooth permission. Allow it in the system settings and try again.
err.ble.connection: The Bluetooth connection to the node failed or was lost. Move closer and try again.
err.ble.connectFailed: Could not connect to {name}. Move closer, check that the node is still in update mode and try again. On Windows, removing an old pairing of the node can help.
err.ble.noBootloader: The node did not switch to update mode. Put it into DFU mode manually and scan again.
err.dfu.timeout: The node stopped answering during the update.
err.dfu.transport: The Bluetooth connection was lost during the update.
err.dfu.package: The firmware file is damaged or not an update package. Download it again.
err.wifi.wrongFamily: This node runs {node}, but the selected file is a {file} firmware. Choose a {node} firmware; switching between the two needs a USB flash.
err.wifi.uploadTimeout: The upload timed out. Check that this device is still on the node's WiFi.
